rationale: A wins because it catches the one question that decides whether the strongest angle survives: "whether the 10% applies to subscriptions bought inside the iOS and Android apps, or whether app-store fees stack on top." B is competent, but its equivalent proof line, "does it include payment-processing costs, or is processing on top?" misses the platform-fee trap hiding inside its own app-store framing. That is the difference between a reporter-proof angle and a pitch that gets dismantled on the first call.
gaps_in_A: "the fee comparison is Discord's own framing" over-attributes the comparison; the update gives the 10% vs. 30% fact, but does not say Discord framed it that way.
"The launch lands while the IPO reporting is live" slightly overstates the supplied fact; the update only says Discord is reportedly preparing for an IPO.

The trend angle still needs outside comparison data before it is pitchable; A admits this, but "The community server becomes the creator's paywall" is thin without the requested comparable platform evidence.
gaps_in_B: "is a direct shot at the prevailing platform-fee structure" turns a pricing comparison into intent. The update does not say Discord is taking a shot at anyone.
"how dependent is Discord on Nitro-style subscriptions today" smuggles in outside company knowledge. Useful question, wrong source discipline for a blind grounded set.
"the person who has run a large gaming community for free" invents both "large" and "for free." The update says server owners can charge; it does not describe their prior economics.
B misses the iOS/Android app-store stacking question in the fee angle. For an app-store comparison, that is not a footnote; it is the trapdoor.
